In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
βAgI disappears in (AgI)x–(NaPO2)x composites at room temperatures with x < 0.8.
βAgI disappears at room temperature in (AgI)-based composites with a high phosphate content.
the oxidation of the phosphate chains in the melt-quenching process is the main reason why βAgI disappears in (AgI)(0.7–)–(NaPO 3)0. 3 at room temperature.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the βAgI phase is stable at room temperature when there are more iodine anions in the composite, but is unstable when the iodine anions are replaced by oxygens in the form of phosphate chains, which are oxidized to phosphate tetrahedrons.
(AgI)–(NaPO) composites are a mixture of AgI and AgPO4, and the AgI phase can be βAgI or Ag5IP2, depending on the Na/P ratio.
the βAgI phase is not stable in the presence of phosphate at room temperature, but it is stable in the presence sulphide, as reported in (Ag2S)0.8-(Na2S)0,2.
